svg.title: Amazon VPC
svg.desc: Amazon VPC. Your private network in AWS: subnets in each Availability Zone, route tables, gateways, security groups and endpoints. Step 1, Where it sits: Public subnets face the internet; ECS tasks and the database sit in private subnets in two zones. Step 2, A request comes in: Shopper → internet gateway → ALB (443) → catalog task (8080 from alb-sg) → RDS (5432 from app-sg). Step 3, Going out: A task's 0.0.0.0/0 route leads to its zone's NAT gateway; traffic to S3 takes the gateway endpoint. Step 4, A zone fails, the limits: Zone a fails and zone b serves on. Limits: NAT cost per hour and per GB, 5 reserved IPs per subnet.

g.text: Public subnets face the internet; ECS tasks and the database sit in private subnets in two zones.
Shopper → internet gateway → ALB (443) → catalog task (8080 from alb-sg) → RDS (5432 from app-sg).
A task's 0.0.0.0/0 route leads to its zone's NAT gateway; traffic to S3 takes the gateway endpoint.
Zone a fails and zone b serves on. Limits: NAT cost per hour and per GB, 5 reserved IPs per subnet.
ONE PRIVATE NETWORK, TWO AVAILABILITY ZONES, THREE TIERS
The VPC spans the Region and every subnet sits in one zone. A subnet is public when its route table sends 0.0.0.0/0 to the internet gateway:
only the ALB nodes and NAT gateways sit there. ECS tasks and the RDS database have private addresses only, which the internet cannot reach.
Other VPCs and the office (over Site-to-Site VPN or Direct Connect) attach to a Transit Gateway; VPC peering links two VPCs directly.
Each hop passes the security group of what it reaches; a rule can name another group instead
of addresses. Groups are stateful: the reply goes back without a rule of its own. Network ACLs
filter whole subnets and are stateless, so they need rules for the return traffic as well.
OUT THROUGH THE NAT GATEWAY, S3 THROUGH THE ENDPOINT
The most specific route wins. nat-b, in the task’s own zone, replaces the private source address,
so the payment API sees nat-b’s Elastic IP. Replies return; nothing outside can open a connection in.
Traffic to S3 matches the prefix-list route: the gateway endpoint is free and skips the NAT gateway.
Zone b has its own ALB node, NAT gateway and tasks: it serves on.
RDS promotes the standby (typically in 60–120 s) and moves its DNS
name; the ALB sends requests to healthy targets in zone b only.
NAT gateway, us-east-1: $0.045 per hour + $0.045 per GB processed
5 addresses reserved per subnet · CIDRs must not overlap networks you join
Default quotas: 60 in + 60 out rules per security group, 5 groups per ENI
